record.provider: Nostr relays as blob transport (event path, not Blossom)

free_tier.stated: no storage quota, but a hard per-event size ceiling that is the real limit. Probed NIP-11 limitation.max_message_length: relay.damus.io 1,000,000 bytes; relay.primal.net 1,000,000 bytes; nos.lol 131,072 bytes. No payment_required, no auth_required on any of the three.

egress.terms: free and unmetered on all three.

record.interface_detail: WebSocket, NIP-01 REQ/EVENT; NIP-94 kind 1063 carries file metadata only.
record.tooling: nak, nostr-tools, any relay client. Blobs are pinned by sha256+url in tags; the bytes live elsewhere (Blossom).
record.chaining: Base64 encoding in tags expands payload size by 4/3, reducing a 1 MB message limit to approximately 750 KB of useful bytes. Storing binary objects in event streams introduces high metadata and encoding overhead.
record.limits_note: per-object-cap ~1 MB on the most generous relays, 128 KB on nos.lol. 1 TiB would be ~1.4 million events.
record.reliability_note: relays can be paid-gated (NIP-11 payment_required) and prune old events; several now require auth for writes. Correct use is metadata only, which is exactly what NIP-94 defines.

evidence.proved: with Accept: application/nostr+json — literal: max_message_length 1000000, max_subscriptions 200, payment_required None, auth_required None
NIP-94 defines kind 1063 file metadata with url/mime/sha256/size tags — metadata, not bytes
'the total size of the event can't be larger than 50 267 340 bytes (~50 MB)' as an upper protocol bound, far above what any public relay accepts
